picks.title: Free, Open Source StemDeck Stem Separator For Linux, Mac & Windows
picks.excerpt: Stemdeck is a modern stem extraction platform, designed to isolate vocals, drums, bass, piano and guitar for practice, transcription, remixing, and creative audio workflows.
picks.rationale: The only shippable tool in the pool: free, open-source, runs locally on all three desktop OSes and pulls five stems including piano and guitar, so a producer can change tomorrow's remix and transcription workflow with no upload and no subscription.

picks.title: Music as a cultural infrastructure business
picks.excerpt: Suno is introducing deliberate friction to pump the brakes on the AI-powered superabundance it helped create, implementing download caps around how much music users can output.
picks.rationale: Hard product news wrapped in analysis: Suno is capping how much music users can download, the first time a generative music platform has designed friction into its own output, which directly changes the economics of prompt-heavy workflows.

picks.title: How Each Music Listening Platform Is Treating AI Music (Updating)
picks.excerpt: From Bandcamp's ban of AI music to Spotify's 'AI Personas,' here's how all the online music platforms are dealing with the flood of AI songs.
picks.rationale: A single maintained map of every DSP and store's AI rules, from Bandcamp's outright ban to Spotify's AI Personas, which is the practical decision sheet for where and how to release an AI-assisted track.

picks.title: 'Human-First' Needs More Than Just a Checkbox
picks.excerpt: Anti-AI music labels need more than self-attestation to function in the real world. An independently administered certification system could be the answer.
picks.rationale: Flips the labelling debate from AI-detection to human-verification, arguing self-attestation cannot hold and proposing an independent certification body, which is the design problem every 'human-made' badge now has to solve.

picks.title: Round Hill joins the AI lawsuit party, targets Suno and Anthropic
picks.excerpt: More lawsuits have been filed against generative AI companies, this time Round Hill suing Suno and Anthropic. Round Hill insists 'there is nothing fair about that use'.
picks.rationale: A music publisher, not a label, opens a new front by suing Suno and Anthropic together, pushing the fair-use fight onto composition rights and lyrics, which is the layer that decides what generative tools may legally output.
